officialAlternative.finding: The exact faculty regulations link redirected to the institutional sign-in page, requesting an account/password and MFA. No authentication attempted. This is missing public academic evidence, not a missing local browser/R dependency.

findings: Fresh English and Dutch curriculum pages explicitly identify 2026–2027 and distinguish previous-year PDFs. Both current-course links identify programme 52637834. The public repository response remains the identical 8,773-byte application shell, with no inspected course-unit credit records.

The public 2025–2026 EER is byte-identical to the earlier review. Article 8.5 makes it effective from 1 September 2025 for academic year 2025–2026. Article 3.6 and the archived course catalogue are preserved as historical subject/credit research; they are not transferred to September 2026 entrants. Its year-three table is expressly subject to change.

Historical EER Article 4.2 requires the full first year plus year-two periods 1–3 before electives abroad; historical thesis entry requires 100 credits including the full first year before 1 September of the thesis year. These rules are read and retained as historical evidence, not promoted to current verified entry conditions.

The current minor menu lists Arts/Heritage, European Studies, Gender/Diversity, Globalisation/Development, Great Thinkers, Sustainable Healthcare, European Public Health, Health Sciences, Sustainability and Art/Law/Policy; Brain Science students must take all 30 credits and obtain faculty/Board approval. Its stated application cycle is 2027–2028, while linked minor documents say 2026–2027. This does not establish September 2026 entrants’ later minor availability or a complete current degree pathway.

The official exchange guidance points to AskPsy and the faculty intranet for EERs. AskPsy gives a 401 information notice and the exact faculty link redirects to institutional sign-in. A reasonable official alternative was followed once; no university contact, login, browser or software installation attempted. Both web search engines located current prospectuses and older formal regulations, without an inspected current credit/regulation replacement.

Current programme purpose is independently confirmed: biology, psychology and computation integrate molecules/cells, synapses/networks, cognition and behaviour; experiments, mathematical models, Python/R, reporting and research/AI ethics are substantive methods. Brain health, lifestyle and brain-disorder treatment are explicit applications. Careers and postgraduate examples do not establish a population-health core.

All 35 exact-target interest rows are unchanged from the prior reviewed case version. Preserve 25 generator roles, seven support topics and three search-only outcomes. Sixteen direct brain/method interests are qualitatively supported by the current programme and why-study pages. Nine distinct minor-associated interests remain individually identified, with cohort-specific availability and construction weight unverified; no omnibus residual direction or fabricated coverage approval.

Current main workbook is unchanged and readable with 151 active courses. All 40 archived course identities, descriptions, prerequisites and topic/description facts match the prior review; both original schedules pass current feasibility. Description-only Advanced Calculus and Perception & Action receive full consideration within their official descriptions.

The neural/computational prototype materially addresses the target through actual neurobiology, cognitive functions, perception/action, biology, maths, programming and statistical/computational methods. Its research remains provisional while the complete external basis is missing. Replaced general body anatomy, whose evidence does not establish specialist neuroanatomy, with Pharmacology’s explicit nervous-system drugs and psychoactive-drug research design. Artificial neural networks remain computational learning tools rather than biological neural simulation.

The population/public-health prototype is rejected as constructed. General health, economics, sociology, policy and biomedicine do not sufficiently preserve this target’s defining neural/cognitive/computational inquiry. A current minor name or healthcare career possibility is not a substitute for programme-level comparability. Its schedule and course facts remain historical, mechanically valid research. No third alternative generated after this rejection and no final one-programme comparison count approved.

essentialMissingEvidence: For September 2026 Brain Science entrants, verify the complete course-unit credit allocation and applicable progression, minor/elective, project and thesis requirements. The public 2025–2026 catalogue/EER and later minor application cycle do not establish this pathway.
confirmedScope: Programme identity, broad academic substance and methods; historical 180-credit degree research retained. No September 2026 component-credit table or complete graduation pathway verified.
